summary: Added a lazy public Files/Search launcher and explicit :Workbench enable/disable/files/search/close commands. Workbench remains disabled by default; opening while disabled does not construct providers or enable it. The host maps Space W to Files and Space / to Search while preserving Space f, with mapping descriptions and lazy command resolvers. Actual host RPC-grid runs on both Neovim versions exercise Files enumeration, a real ripgrep query, rendered results, focus, disable cleanup and modified-buffer preservation at all four grids. Both optional Nix source-installation paths built with the local runtime staged as an override, and the configured macOS system derivation built under WITH_NVIM=1 without activation. WB-25 remains incomplete because the runtime is unpublished: the locked upstream input is still planning-only, so exact runtime pin parity, clean recursive install and rollout/activation evidence remain outstanding.

gates.command: make check-ownership; inspect docs/tasks.json#WB-25, changed repository paths and the Workbench runtime scope inventory
gates.result: Ownership validation passed for 39 Workbench Lua modules. The Workbench runtime owns and disposes the layout, Files/Search controllers, filesystem/ripgrep providers, result store and navigation service through one scope; it constructs them only on an enabled open. The host init uses lazy require closures and does not import controllers. WB-25 allowed paths were extended to include the missing public facade/runtime boundary and its runtime/E2E tests.

gates.command: make test NVIM_CURRENT=nvim; sh ../autoconf.nvim/tests/run.sh; make test-integration; make check-ownership; tests/e2e/wb25_host.py on minimum/current Neovim
gates.result: All 161 Workbench mini.test cases passed on Neovim 0.11.7 and 0.12.4, including the public host lifecycle test. Autoconf repair, Workbench settings-adapter and optional-dependency suites passed on both versions. All 21 Python integration/plan tests passed; planning structure and import ownership checks passed. The eight public host RPC-grid scenarios also passed.

gates.command: make test NVIM_CURRENT=nvim; tests/e2e/wb25_host.py --grid-sizes 160x50,120x35,80x24,60x20 on both Neovim versions
gates.result: The public-runtime test verifies that pre-setup and explicitly disabled opens return structured errors without constructing runtime resources; three enable/open/disable cycles leave Workbench disabled with runtime nil. Each real-grid host run opens both views then disables them, restores the original editor window/buffer, and preserves modified user text. The internal suite passed its cancellation, stale-result and resource-disposal cases.

All four actual terminal grids passed on both versions. Space W visibly opens Files and enumerates note.txt; Space / opens Search, actual /needle input returns one real ripgrep match in the rendered Search buffer, and Search retains focus. The 60x20 overlay works. Space f remains mapped; Space / deliberately replaces the prior global-search binding.

gates.command: .test-deps/venv/bin/python bench/startup.py --runs 20 --nvim nvim; inspect WB-25 host E2E timing records
gates.result: Twenty interleaved warm host/plugin-free pairs measured host startup marker p50/p95 42.477/43.171 ms, process wall 62.349/63.632 ms and first UI frame 58.624/61.763 ms, all below the 150 ms startup budget. Across the latest eight actual-grid Workbench runs, Space W to first visible flush measured 53.262–63.188 ms, including live provider work at all four terminal sizes. The dormant Workbench startup profile remains covered by the E2E checks and does not construct its runtime/providers.

gates.result: Minimum/current Neovim, standalone runtime, Autoconf settings adapter, optional-dependency, integration, UI and ownership tests passed. gates.command: git ls-remote --symref git@github.com:OlegHQ/workbench.nvim.git HEAD 'refs/heads/*' 'refs/tags/*'; git ls-remote --symref git@github.com:OlegHQ/nvim-config.git HEAD refs/heads/dev; inspect local Nix lock, recursive-clone parity and activation state
gates.result: The opt-in Nix standalone and configured macOS system builds passed only with the local unpublished runtime supplied via path overrides. The checked-in flake.lock resolves Workbench to published planning-only SHA 0534135d877ec3679bb91ee0b4a68b71e174ff7a, so it is not runtime-parity evidence. The Workbench runtime remains dirty and no commits, pushes or publication were authorized; a clean recursive clone cannot include it. Host activation was not authorized and was not run. Next gate requires publication/pinning of the runtime and parent gitlink, fresh-clone parity validation, and a separately authorized activation/rollback walkthrough. Neovim's Nix path is optional via WITH_NVIM=1 and is not the default host setup.
